newsitem.title: USA: Sacramento, Calif., nears deal with Kings on loan.
newsitem.headline: Sacramento, Calif., nears deal with Kings on loan.

text.p: Sacramento, Calif., officials are finalizing a proposal to issue at least $70 million of bonds to ensure that the National Basketball Association's Sacramento Kings team will remain in the city, officials said on Wednesday.

Under the terms of the proposal, which has yet to be approved by the city council, the owner of the Kings would receive the loan in order to retire debt in a local arena, Bill Farley, the city's economic development manager, said.
In return, Kings owner Jim Thomas would agree to keep his team in Sacramento for 30 years, though he could move the team after 10 years once he repays the loan in full.

The $70-million-plus bond issue, payable over 30 years, would be backed by revenues from Arco Arena. The city would collect over 40 percent -- or about $3.5 million a year -- in revenues from the arena to pay off the bonds, Farley said.

City officials planned to work through details of the proposal with the city's investment bankers in the coming days. They hoped to bring the $70 million proposal to the city council next week and to hold a public hearing on the issue.
If it is approved by the city council, the city could come to market with the bonds in April or May, Farley said.
"The financing is intended to be a very strong loan that will be a really good deal from a local government perspective," Farley said.
Thomas had sought $90 million to retire his debt in the arena and team. Without a financial commitment from Sacramento, he warned that he might be forced to move the team to another city.
